claims.text: Adding Pd to a NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloy narrows the distribution of exchange interaction energies.
A narrowed distribution of exchange interaction energies promotes a continuous, second-order magnetic transition at low applied fields.
Pd tuning enhances the magnetic entropy change of the alloy.
Pd tuning preserves rapid heat exchange and mechanical stability.
The NiFeCoCr baseline with minimal or no Pd has a relatively broad distribution of exchange interactions.
Pd content will be systematically varied in NiFeCoCrPdx while the other compositional factors are held constant.
The samples will be produced by arc melting followed by a homogenizing heat treatment below the melting point.
Measurements will cover 100–400 K and applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
An optimal Pd addition enhances chemical homogeneity.
Pd selectively modifies local electronic environments and exchange interactions.
The Pd-induced changes in local electronic environments and exchange interactions cause a second-order magnetic transition with reduced hysteresis.
An optimal Pd concentration will produce a sharper but continuous magnetic transition relative to the baseline.
An optimal Pd concentration will produce a larger low-field magnetic entropy change relative to the baseline.
An optimal Pd concentration will reduce hysteresis losses relative to the baseline.
An optimal Pd concentration will not degrade thermal conductivity relative to the baseline.
An optimal Pd concentration will not degrade mechanical performance relative to the baseline.
The proposed behavior is limited to NiFeCoCrPdx compositions near the eventual optimum, temperatures near the magnetic transition within 100–400 K, and fields below 1 T.
